evidence: Cic. de Or. 3.53; Cic. Or. 39; Quint. 9.1 (Lewis & Short: “rhet. t. t., a figure of speech”, Greek σχῆμα)
terms.comment: The rhetoricians’ term for any figure of speech, rendering Greek σχῆμα; a metaphor is trānslātiō, and a trope tropus.

terms.gloss: metaphor, a word used in a transferred sense
evidence: Cic. de Or. 3.38.156: trānslātiōnēs audāciōrēs (Lewis & Short: “a trope, metaphor”)
terms.comment: Narrower than “figure of speech”: the metaphor only.
Cicero has figūra ōrātiōnis of a style of speaking, full or plain (de Or. 3.55.212, Lewis & Short), not of a single figure. We have found no classical instance of the phrase in Traupman’s sense.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 314; p. 315.
